title: Flow and decisions: how work moves and how decisions settle

sections.name: summary
sections.label: In short
sections.content: Four models of how work moves through the programme and one of how decisions settle, compared and not yet tested against cases.

sections.name: models
sections.label: The models
sections.content:
- The archetypal flow (2026-10-25): nine stages, each what we are trying to achieve, in order: Sense, Make meaning, Choose a response, Shape the work, Allocate, Build, Review and land, Decide, Learn and remember. Each stage is a subdomain of Programme coordination with one trade-off and an exercise of what we tried. It is the ideal layer.
- Flow model B (2026-10-25): an independent model made to compare against the first.
- Programme coordination by seven questions (2026-10-25): the domain mapped by the questions it must answer, with its clusters, problems and remedies.
- The decision flow (2026-10-28): stage 8, Decide, zoomed in: Arise, Settle by principle, Place, Decide, Record, Cite and revisit.
- Comparing the flow models: what the models agree and disagree on.

sections.name: state
sections.label: Where it stands
sections.content: The stage trade-offs are untested: no 2x2 cases yet. The next action is to fill the four cases for one stage's trade-off with the owner (Review and land is the best evidenced). Flow stops and decision stops are recorded as findings against the stages (tags flow-stop and decision-stop). The stages are also laid out as domains in the domain map.

sections.name: drill
sections.label: How to read it
sections.content: Each model below is its own section. Inside the archetypal flow, each stage has its exercise, its trade-off and the two poles with their shadows; the owner's vignettes sit under the exercise they shaped.
